description:
Domains whose registration, first certificate and first DNS answer cluster inside a short window: the shape of infrastructure stood up in one go. NEEDS AN API KEY ON THE PRO PLAN.

max_hours_to_cert bounds registration to certificate and cert_to_dns_max bounds certificate to first answer, both in hours. first_dns_answer is bounded by our own scan latency, so within 24 hours of registration only some candidates have one yet; the reply's coverage says how many. tld, ns, since and until narrow it; page with after=<next_cursor>. A tight cluster is a pattern, not a finding.

Defaults: the last 72 hours, max_hours_to_cert 6 (ceiling 168), 100 rows per page (maximum 500). Each row gives domain, tld, first_zone_seen, first_cert_seen, first_dns_answer, dns_status, hours_zone_to_cert (negative when the certificate came first), hours_cert_to_dns, sequence, cert_id and ns. scanned above count means filters removed rows after the page was drawn, so a short page is not the end. For newly registered domains without the timing filter use new_domains.

after.description: The next_cursor from the previous call.

cert_to_dns_max.description: First certificate to first DNS answer, at most this many hours.

include_cert_before_zone.description: Also include domains certified BEFORE a zone file listed them (sequence cert_before_zone). Default false.

max_hours_to_cert.description: Registration to first certificate, at most this many hours. Default 6, maximum 168.

ns.description: Only domains delegated to this nameserver.

since.description: Window start, RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD, UTC. Default 72 hours back.

tld.description: Only this TLD, without the dot, e.g. "xyz".

until.description: Window end, RFC3339 or YYYY-MM-DD, UTC. Default now.

name: provisioning
title: Domains provisioned in one burst
